entries.detail:
DEP-001's subject is "the change made this session," so per the audit instructions I read the written record at /Users/scottlydon/Developer/GOAL_LOOP_INTERSTICE_HANGS_AND_AKIN_SOCIAL_2026-08-19_NOTES.md in full (356 lines) rather than guessing, since that file and the goal loop beside it are the only account of the session available to me. I could not find DEP-004..DEP-013 row results anywhere for this session (they are this row's stated input per the CSV's deterministic_tools column), so this row cannot legitimately PASS.

Section "What swath N1 shipped" (line 87) declares nine test classes and 22 fixed defects (later itemized as 27 total, section "9.5 Defects fixed in this loop", table around line 145) as complete, and section "4.13 closed, and why it was open" (line 300) explicitly closes items on the strength of `swift test --package-path $SRV` going from 2 failures to 0 failures locally, with git status clean and commits pushed. Per the B,F2 row of the cross-document sweep (line 271), the deployment target for this repository is Render, with migrations run by hand from the service shell. Nowhere in the notes is there any git push to a Render deploy branch, any build-log confirmation, any service restart, or any curl against a live/staging URL proving the 27 fixed defects are observable in a running deployed instance. Everything reported as "shipped," "closed," or "fixed" in this session is backed only by local `swift test` and `git status` evidence, which the deployment matrix (row for external hosts) explicitly says is NOT sufficient ("auto-deploy is NOT the same as deployed-and-verified"). I also checked the akin-server-side target files directly (Dockerfile, scripts/, README.md, CLAUDE.md, Sources/App/Configuration) but their mtimes are all a uniform Aug 21 15:49 (a checkout artifact, not evidence of this session's edits), so they add no deployment evidence either way; the notes file remains the only reliable account.

FAIL: no DEP-004..DEP-013 evidence, and no build/deploy/restart/curl step recorded anywhere in the session's own written record for the akin-server-side changes it repeatedly calls "shipped" and "closed."
entries.rule_title: Code edited is not code shipped

None of the targets match that shape. /Users/scottlydon/Developer/akin-server-side/Dockerfile confirms the backend is Swift/Vapor ("FROM swift:6.0-focal", COPY ./Package.*), and scripts/server-up.sh / server-down.sh show it is managed with a recorded PID file + graceful SIGTERM/SIGKILL fallback, not the pkill -9 -f pattern this rule specifies; the goal-loop notes (the only account of this session, /Users/scottlydon/Developer/GOAL_LOOP_INTERSTICE_HANGS_AND_AKIN_SOCIAL_2026-08-19_NOTES.md, line 271) further record the deployment target as Render with migrations run by hand from the service shell, i.e. a hosted-platform deploy path, not a local process restart. /Users/scottlydon/Developer/interstice/bin/interstice.js and lib/install.js are a Node CLI/daemon installer (start/stop/status subcommands, LaunchAgent-based), not a "server/" backend with a local pkill+curl health-check deploy flow. I grepped the notes file for pkill, nohup, restart, daemon, launchagent, install.js, interstice.js, deploy, npm run, systemctl and found no record of any backend source change being deployed through the kill -9/restart/health-check sequence this rule checks, so there is nothing in scope for this rule to pass or fail against in either the targets or the session record."

entries.detail: DEP-009 requires (a) running the migration, (b) verifying the schema change with a live query, (c) exercising the app path that reads it, and calls out that Render never auto-runs migrations so this must be done through the Render Web Shell. My audit constraints forbid running builds, migrations, or a test suite, so I could not execute any of (a)-(c) myself; that gap is the finding, not an assumption of pass. I read scripts/migrate.sh, scripts/server-up.sh, CLAUDE.md:19-39, README.md:13-50, and Sources/App/Configuration/configure.swift:303-346, which together show migrations run two ways here: manually via `./Run migrate --yes` (CLAUDE.md:25-26, 39; README.md:50, Render Web Shell per the rule's own note) and automatically at boot via `app.autoMigrate()` when `DEPLOYMENT == debug` (configure.swift:342-346), which per the code's own comment (configure.swift:328-336) is true for BOTH the staging and production Render services. The only live evidence available is in the session record at /Users/scottlydon/Developer/GOAL_LOOP_INTERSTICE_HANGS_AND_AKIN_SOCIAL_2026-08-19_NOTES.md lines 312-342: a 2026-08-21 run migrated a fresh local/CI database (`AKIN_TEST_DB`), then queried `\d entitlements` (schema verified: table present with id, user_id, capability, created_at) and confirmed `ContextModerationTests.testCleanNameCreatesContextAndRecordsAssessment` read a row back (app-reads verified). The notes explicitly say this ran against the test suite's fresh database, not `$DATABASE_URL`/the deployed Render service, because no `DATABASE_URL` was exported locally (lines 340-342). So no step in this audit, and no account in the only session record available, shows the migration being run, queried, and exercised against the actual deployed (Render) database that CLAUDE.md:39 and README.md:50 describe, which is the specific scenario the rule calls out by name. I am reporting this as a finding against my own coverage rather than asserting a pass I did not verify.
entries.rule_title: Database migration: run it, verify the schema, verify the app reads it

entries.detail: akin-server-side's CLAUDE.md line 10 and README.md lines 41-48 document the hosted deploy: Render builds from GitHub main and serves https://akin-server-side.onrender.com. Running `git fetch origin` then `git status -sb` and `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` in /Users/scottlydon/Developer/akin-server-side showed `## main...origin/main [ahead 1]` with unpushed commit `b501bb4 Stop logging stored password digests` (local HEAD b501bb4b87ab..., origin/main 9af76379ae95...). That commit was never git-pushed to the deploy branch, so no build could have run for it and it cannot be live. `curl -s --max-time 10 https://akin-server-side.onrender.com/` returned `HTTP 200` / `welcome to the api!`, proving only that whatever commit IS currently deployed is up, not that this newest local commit (a password-digest-logging removal, i.e. security-relevant) shipped. Per DEP-013 this is a violation: step (a) git push never happened for this commit, so steps (b) watch the build log and (c) curl-verify-the-new-code could not and did not happen either. This is a live git/host-state finding on the deployed system itself, not a reconstruction from the session notes (DEP-013's SUBJECT is the deployed system, not the transcript, so I audited the repo/host directly rather than deferring to GOAL_LOOP_INTERSTICE_HANGS_AND_AKIN_SOCIAL_2026-08-19_NOTES.md). Also checked: /Users/scottlydon/Developer/interstice/lib/install.js and bin/interstice.js (grep -niE 'render|vercel|firebase|deploy' returned no hits) are a local CLI/LaunchAgent tool with no hosted-deploy surface, and akin-server-side's Dockerfile/scripts/Sources/App/Configuration are the build/local-dev artifacts, not the host config itself (no render.yaml present) so DEP-013 applies only via CLAUDE.md/README's documented Render target, where the finding above holds.
entries.rule_title: Hosted deploy: push, watch the build log, curl the deployed URL

entries.detail: The old Hostinger VPS service at 5.183.11.8 is documented as "retired" in the README's "Historical note" section, but it is still responding with HTTP 200. The rule requires superseded services to be both suspended (offline) and noted in the README to prevent users from mistaking stale links for the live product. This service violates DEP-017 because it is not actually suspended, only documented as historical. A user could still access the old service and become confused about which deployment is the canonical one.
entries.rule_title: One canonical user-facing URL; superseded services are suspended and noted
